events.label: Hill approaching
events.detail: A guided-workout incline change is approaching.

events.label: Steady effort
events.detail: You have settled into a consistent rhythm.

start: You showed up. That's a good start. Settle into a pace that feels right for you.
One step at a time. Find your rhythm. I'm right here with you.
Give yourself a gentle opening few minutes. You can build the effort once you feel settled.
Today's goal is to find an effort you can sustain. Start easy and let your rhythm come to you.
hill: There's a hill coming up. Shorten your stride, stay tall, and choose a pace you can control.
An incline is coming. You don't have to rush it. Take the hill one steady step at a time.
An uphill section is next. Keep your steps comfortable and let your speed match the extra effort.
We have a climb ahead. Relax your hands, look forward, and take it one step at a time.
steady: That's a lovely rhythm. Relax your shoulders and keep breathing.
You're being consistent. That effort adds up, even when it feels ordinary.
Let your hands relax. You can keep working without carrying tension in your fists.
Check your posture. Look ahead and let your shoulders settle comfortably.
Find a comfortable breathing rhythm. If the effort feels too much, ease the pace.
Keep your steps smooth. You don't need to reach far out in front of you.
Check in with yourself. A little adjustment now can help the next few minutes feel better.
Consistency is built in moments like this. Stay with an effort that works for you.
push: You've got more in you if you're feeling good. Choose your next effort. You're in charge.
You're doing the work. If you want a little more, build it gradually.
Think about why you made time for this today. Every comfortable step is part of that commitment.
You don't need a personal best today. Showing up and doing the work is progress.
Focus on this minute. You can decide what the next one needs when you get there.
Notice one thing that feels stronger or more comfortable than when you started.
You're building a habit with every session. This effort belongs to you.
If you're feeling strong, enjoy it. If today is harder, adjusting the pace is still moving forward.
mile: Another mile done. Give yourself credit. You earned every step.
That's another mile in the bank. Look at what you've already done.
You've completed a mile. Check your breathing, take stock of your effort, and give yourself some credit.
Another mile completed. Stay with your own pace and enjoy that progress.
recovery: Take this recovery. An easier pace is part of the workout, too.
Let your breathing settle. There's nothing to prove during recovery.
Recovery gives you a chance to let the effort settle before the next part. Keep this section easy.
An easy interval helps you manage the whole workout. Let your breathing come back under control.
finish: Workout complete. You made time for yourself today. Well done.
You stayed with it. Enjoy the cool-down. That was your work, and it counts.
That's the end of the session. Take an easy cool-down before you step off.
Session finished. You gave yourself time to move today, and that matters.

personalities.name: Pace Coach
personalities.tagline: Permission to slow down. Progress at your pace.

start: Begin gently. Let your steps find a comfortable rhythm.
Be here for this step. Then the next. There is no rush.
Start with a pace that feels easy. There is no need to decide the whole workout right now.
Give yourself time to warm up. A comfortable walk is a perfectly good place to begin.
hill: A hill is coming. You can slow down or walk the climb. There is no need to hold the same speed uphill.
The incline is changing. Choose a comfortable effort. Taking it slower is a valid choice.
There's an uphill section ahead. You can ease your speed before the climb begins.
A climb is coming. Keep the effort comfortable, even if that means taking it much slower.
steady: This pace is enough. You do not have to go faster for your effort to count.
Listen to how you feel. You can stay here, ease back, or take a break.
Unclench your hands and soften your shoulders. Let your steps feel unhurried.
Try looking ahead instead of down. Find a posture that feels comfortable.
Check your breathing. If you'd prefer a little more ease, slow the pace.
You can walk for the rest of this session. There is nothing you have to prove.
Pay attention to how your body feels today. The plan can adapt to you.
Let the next few minutes be simple. Comfortable steps and a manageable effort are enough.
push: It is okay to slow down. Walking counts. Choose a pace that feels manageable today.
You do not have to earn a recovery break. Ease back when you need to. This is your workout.
Rest and easier days belong in a routine too. You can adjust your goal without losing your progress.
Your pace doesn't need to match anyone else's. Choose what feels right for this minute.
A shorter session can still be worthwhile. You get to decide when you've done enough.
You can be proud of making time for movement without chasing a faster number.
If the day has taken a lot out of you, give yourself an easier workout.
You don't have to finish the way you started. Slowing down is an option whenever you need it.
mile: One more mile behind you. Take a breath and acknowledge it.
Another milestone. No hurry. Just progress.
A mile completed at your own pace. Take a moment to appreciate it.
Another mile is behind you. You can keep going gently, or begin winding down.
recovery: Ease back. Recovery is part of the rhythm.
Let your breathing settle. Keep this interval comfortable.
This easier interval lets the effort settle. Recovery is part of training, not a failure to keep going.
Use this recovery to find comfortable breathing again. An easy pace helps you manage what comes next.
finish: Your session is complete. Finish gently. You have done enough for today.
The work is finished. Take your time coming back to stillness.
Your workout has ended. Give yourself an easy cool-down and time to settle.
That's your session complete. However far you went, you made time for yourself.

start: Alright, you lazy fuck. You showed up. Now put some purpose into those steps. Pick a pace you can handle.
Get your ass moving. This workout isn't going to do itself. Start controlled, then earn the effort.
Time to get your ass in gear. Warm up first. A smart start beats a stupid sprint.
You're here, so make it count. Start easy, find your rhythm, and bring some damn focus.
hill: Hill coming up. Get your shit together, shoulders back, short steps. Take that climb at a pace you can own.
Here's the damn hill. Focus up. You don't need a miracle, you need the next solid step.
Climb ahead. Short steps, relaxed shoulders. Pick an effort you can handle and own the damn hill.
Here comes the uphill. Don't let your ego pick the speed. Stay controlled and get the job done.
steady: There you go. That's some actual fucking consistency. Stay focused and own that rhythm.
Look at you putting in the work. Keep your shit together and stay smooth.
Unclench those damn fists. Put that energy into smooth steps instead.
Shoulders down, eyes forward. Get your posture together and keep this controlled.
Check your breathing. If you're overcooking it, back the hell off and find your rhythm.
Smooth steps. You're training, not trying to stomp a hole through the damn deck.
Pay attention to how you feel. Discipline includes adjusting the plan when you need to.
Stay with this minute. Consistency is boring as hell sometimes, and it still gets the work done.
push: Come on, you lazy fuck, you can do better if you've got it today. Choose a controlled effort and commit.
Less bullshit, more purpose. Pick your next minute and make every damn step count.
You made time for this. Give the next minute some purpose, whatever pace you've chosen.
Stop arguing with the clock. One damn step, then the next. That's the job.
Nobody needs a heroic sprint. Give me an honest, controlled effort.
This is how habits get built. Show up, do the work, and repeat the damn thing.
If you've got more today, build gradually. If you haven't, quit the ego bullshit and hold a manageable pace.
Look at the work you've already put in. That didn't happen by sitting on your ass.
mile: Another fucking mile. You earned that. Don't let anyone tell you that effort doesn't count.
Mile done. That's your work right there. Not luck, not excuses. Your damn work.
A full damn mile completed. Check your effort and take the win.
Another mile in the books. That's earned progress. Keep your next steps controlled.
recovery: Take the fucking recovery. Training smart is part of the job. Breathe and reset.
Ease back. This is the recovery interval, not an ego contest. Do the damn plan.
Recovery lets the effort settle so you can manage the rest of the workout. Take the damn easy interval seriously.
Back off and get your breathing comfortable. Recovery is in the plan for a reason. Follow the fucking plan.
finish: You finished the fucking workout. That's how it's done. Cool down and take the win.
Work done. No more excuses today. You showed up and delivered. Now cool down properly.
Session complete. You did the damn work. Now give yourself an easy cool-down.
That's the workout finished. Take the win, cool down, and come back ready for another day.
